baselineQuestions.text: Did leaving the top backup roll balance isolated in a 'raised' position change the load path or mechanical restraint on the yoke/carrier beam compared to its normal operating configuration?
baselineQuestions.rationale: If yes, this suggests an equipment state dependency that broke during outage prep. If no, focus shifts to hydraulic pressure loss effects.
evidenceNeeded: Mechanical assembly drawing of R3 carrier beam/yoke/roll balance interface
Maintenance procedure for roll removal and isolation

baselineQuestions.text: Does de-energizing and bleeding the 'B hydraulics' system remove hydraulic support that was actively restraining the carrier beam link/keeper assembly?
baselineQuestions.rationale: If yes, this points to an energy isolation procedure gap where depressurization inadvertently released a mechanical restraint. If no, focus shifts to gravity/mechanical failure.
evidenceNeeded: P&ID or schematic of B hydraulics circuit relative to yoke/carrier beam
Energy Isolation Plan (ECP) for R3 area showing hydraulic boundaries

baselineQuestions.text: Was there a documented handover or inspection confirming the carrier beam remained securely seated and that no unintended changes occurred during the previous shift's outage prep?
baselineQuestions.rationale: If missing, this indicates an administrative control failure. If present but ignored, it points to human error in verification.
evidenceNeeded: Shift turnover log
Area manager notes
Outage work scope documentation
